source.title: The Interpolating Information Criterion for Overparameterized Models
source.authors: Liam Hodgkinson; Christopher van der Heide; Roberto Salomone; Fred Roosta; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error across model-size changes in random Fourier feature, polynomial, and diagonal linear neural network models. This bears on general double descent, but it is not a direct reproduction of the original deep-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The random Fourier feature MNIST experiment explicitly reports a double-descent test-MSE curve. The polynomial regression results explicitly report no double descent and provide test-MSE values by node count. The diagonal linear neural network figure plots test MSE against feature dimension, but the text does not describe its curve shape. Excluded IIC/BIC values and gamma-regression results reporting IIC–test-NLL correlation: they do not report a double-descent outcome. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 6.1 reruns the Belkin et al. random-Fourier-feature MNIST setup (n = 1000, 1–3000 features) and reports test MSE, which bears on V4. Figure 4 sweeps polynomial degree at a fixed 10 nodes and reports test MSE with no second descent, which bears on V4's generality across model classes. The paper's main aim is an information criterion, but these test-error curves are its own results.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors derive the IIC from Bayesian duality and argue the duality helps explain double descent. They show that classical BIC (underparameterized side) plus IIC (overparameterized side) together reproduce the RFF double-descent curve. The IIC also predicts that polynomial interpolators show no second descent, and it correlates with a regularizer-adjusted MSE for diagonal linear networks.
record.recipe_differences: Empirical comparisons use random Fourier features, polynomial regression, and diagonal linear neural networks rather than reproducing the original deep-network model-size experiments; the study also focuses on information-criterion behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported polynomial test errors differ by node choice (equally-spaced versus Chebyshev); outcomes also vary across model classes.

fits_no_version.finding: The IIC tracks test error: it falls monotonically for RFF when d > n, correlates with gamma-regression test NLL (r = 0.996), and correlates with a rescaled DLNN MSE (r = 0.98, versus 0.35 for raw MSE).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A marginal-likelihood-based information criterion for interpolators reproduces the second-descent branch of test error.

record.problems: The random Fourier feature test-error curve is reported only graphically, without curve values. The diagonal linear neural network test-MSE curve is also graphical and its shape is not described in the text. The polynomial table varies n and degree together (d = n + 1), rather than varying model size at fixed sample size.
record.rows_left_out: IIC/BIC curves and values in Figures 2 and 4 and Table 1 were not included because they are information criteria, not test-error results for the claim. Gamma-regression test-NLL/IIC correlation in Figure 3 and text was left out because the study does not report a double-descent outcome there.

untested.parts: Model classes other than random Fourier features and monomial polynomials; whether the curve subsumes the classical U-shape.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Effects of noise or regularization on the peak; multiple descent.
Recounting parameters to turn the second descent into a U-shaped curve.

missing.what: Test MSE (log) of polynomial regression against degree (about 10 to 1000) at a fixed 10 equally spaced nodes; the authors state no double descent appears.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 1 rows are a comparison of node choices at d = n + 1, not capacity sweeps, so they were unlinked. The usable polynomial result for V4 is Figure 4, which no row records. The RFF experiment closely follows the original Belkin setup.

versions.untested_parts: Whether more training samples raise test error near the interpolation threshold.
The study does not test all model classes or establish a general result for all capacity measures.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Whether noise or regularization drives the peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimal regularization removes them.
Whether an effective parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
